newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Thursday, but buying interest was thin despite gains in Malaysia, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,445-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were mostly at the lower end of the range. Crude palm oil was last done at around 1,252 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran city of Medan.

"Demand was weak, with most players seeking to buy at 1,430-35 rupiah," one trader said. "Buyers are only buying what they need because they do not want to build up stocks ahead of the general election in case of any social unrest."
Indonesians go to the polls on May 29, with the ruling Golkar party widely expected to emerge victorious.
The traders said export prices were still at a premium to local levels, adding this should keep local values stable.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Golden Ocean will leave the port on Friday for Madras, India, with 3,500 tonnes of palm oil. The MT Pangeran will leave for Tanjung Priok in Jakarta today with 1,600 tonnes of palm olein. The MT Bobo-IV will leave for Tanjung Priok on Friday with 5,000 tonnes olein.
